transcript.text: My Dyson V10 Absolute (SV12) won't run at all now. On the battery display there's a red light flashing when I press the trigger, then nothing. It was charging overnight. Do I need a new battery or is the whole thing dead?

To answer your question first: a flashing red light usually means the battery protection system has kicked in (often due to overheating from a blockage) or the battery is too low to start. It doesn't necessarily mean the whole thing is dead. The most common cause for this specific symptom on a V10 is that the vacuum got hot during use and triggered a safety cut-out, or there is a blockage restricting airflow. Please try this simple check: put the vacuum back on its charger. Does a solid amber light appear to show it is charging? If yes, leave it for 3-4 hours, then try turning it on again in normal mode (not boost). If no light appears at all when plugged in, we need to look at the charger or battery.

When it's on the charger the blue lights come on, not amber, and then it sometimes shows the flashing red too. I did charge it for over 3.5 hours straight from the charger and it still just flashes red when I press the trigger. Filter was washed last month and there are no blockages.

Since it has been charged for over 3.5 hours and still flashes red without running, the battery protection circuit is likely preventing power delivery due to a failed cell. The blue lights indicate it is receiving some charge, but the flashing red on start-up suggests the battery cannot sustain the load. You will need a replacement battery; this is a standard wear part for cordless vacuums and not a fault with the main unit itself.
